projectSummary: A machine press differs measurably from a barbell bench press in clavicular pectoralis activation at a matched relative load. This is portion-resolved tier-4 evidence that the implement and the grip change which part of the muscle is loaded, and it supports no statement about a cable fly.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: The comparison changes body position as well as implement, so implement and trunk orientation are confounded.
Activation values near 25-30 per cent of MVIC at 60 per cent of 1RM are modest, and the between-exercise difference is small in absolute terms.

study.intervention: horizontal bench press, prone grip at 150 and 50 per cent of biacromial width; seated chest press machine, three grips
study.population: Muscle activity of the clavicular and lower pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii was compared during a horizontal bench press with a prone grip at 150 and 50 per cent of biacromial width and a seated chest press with neutral, prone and supine grips, in sets of 8 repetitions at 60 per cent of 1RM.

title: Comparison of Muscle Activity between the Horizontal Bench Press and the Seated Chest Press Exercises Using Several Grips.
